To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the polarization observables in the pion photo-production from the neutron are in agreement with previous measurements and the theoretical calculations, but not with the world average of the cross sections; 2) the polarization observability in the eta meson photo-production is in agreement with previous data, but not with theory; 3) the polarization observable in the eta' meson photo-production are the first ever measurements of such quantities and the cross sections are in agreement with the theoretical calculations;
the data from our experiments are consistent with the predictions from the MAID 2007 and SAID 2011 partial-wave analyses.

we have measured the polarization transfer coefficients in the reaction $\gamma p \to \pi^{0} p$, for photon energies from the threshold up to 1.4 GeV, and that we have measured, in the same energy range, the polarization transfer coefficients and the beam asymmetry for the reaction $\gamma n \to \pi^{-} p$.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the strong interaction, in particular with the investigation of its fundamental properties, such as chiral symmetry, confinement, and the role played by quarks and gluons in the hadronic spectrum.
the extraction of the S11(1535) and S11(1650) resonances parameters, and with the study of the D13(1520) resonance in the N* -> K*Lambda channel.
the study of the nucleon structure through the investigation of the meson production channels, and in particular of the role played by the resonances.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are now able to extract the resonance contributions to the total and partial cross-sections, and that the polarization observables, in particular the photon asymmetries, are in good agreement with the theoretical calculations, which include the resonance contribution.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the polarization observables provide an additional constraint on the resonance parameter extraction, and that a complete experiment is necessary to fully constrain the resonance model.
